title: The Holy Quran
lines: Islamiat questions on the Quran in USAT ask about how it was revealed and compiled, its structure, the names and themes of well-known surahs, the prophets it mentions, and its main teachings. The questions test stable facts, so a clear timeline and a few tables cover most of them.
## Revelation
- The Quran is the word of Allah, revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) through the angel Jibreel (AS).

- The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira, on Jabal an-Nur near Makkah, in the month of Ramadan, when the Prophet (PBUH) was about 40 years old (610 CE). The first verses revealed were the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, which begin with the command to read.

- Revelation continued gradually for about 23 years: about 13 years in Makkah and 10 in Madinah. The Quran itself explains that gradual revelation strengthened the Prophet's heart and let believers learn step by step.
- The night on which revelation began is Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, described in Surah Al-Qadr as better than a thousand months.
- The Quran was revealed in Arabic. The word Quran means "recitation" or "that which is read". Other names used in the Quran include Al-Furqan (the Criterion) and Adh-Dhikr (the Reminder).
## Makki and Madani surahs
| Makki (before the Hijrah) | Madani (after the Hijrah)
| mostly shorter surahs and verses | mostly longer surahs and verses
| themes: Tawhid, the hereafter, prophethood, stories of earlier nations | themes: laws of worship, family, trade, community, war and peace
| examples: Al-Alaq, Al-Muddaththir, Yasin, Al-Kahf | examples: Al-Baqarah, Aal-Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Hujurat
## Compilation
- In the Prophet's (PBUH) lifetime, the Quran was memorised by many companions and written by scribes on parchment, bone, palm leaves and stones. Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) was a leading scribe.
- After many memorisers were martyred at the Battle of Yamamah (11-12 AH), Umar (RA) urged Abu Bakr (RA) to gather the Quran into one copy. Abu Bakr (RA) gave the task to Zayd ibn Thabit (RA).
- That copy stayed with Abu Bakr (RA), then Umar (RA), and then with Hafsa (RA), the daughter of Umar and a wife of the Prophet (PBUH).

- Uthman (RA) had standard copies prepared from Hafsa's copy and sent them to the main cities, so that all Muslims recited in one agreed form. For this he is called Jami' al-Quran (the gatherer of the Quran).
## Structure in numbers
| Fact | Value
| Surahs | 114
| Paras (juz) | 30
| Longest surah | Al-Baqarah, 286 verses
| Shortest surah | Al-Kawthar, 3 verses
| Opening surah | Al-Fatiha (Umm al-Kitab), 7 verses
| Surah without Bismillah at the start | At-Tawbah
| Bismillah occurring twice | An-Naml
| Surah named after a woman | Maryam
| Last two surahs (Al-Mu'awwidhatayn) | Al-Falaq and An-Nas
## Revealed books and prophets
| Book | Prophet
| Tawrat (Torah) | Musa (AS)
| Zabur (Psalms) | Dawud (AS)
| Injil (Gospel) | Isa (AS)
| Quran | Muhammad (PBUH)

The Quran also mentions scrolls (suhuf) given to Ibrahim (AS) and Musa (AS). It names 25 prophets, among them Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub, Yusuf, Musa, Harun, Dawud, Sulaiman, Yunus, Isa and Muhammad (peace be upon them).
## Stories and teachings often asked
- Nuh (AS) built the ark; Hud (AS) was sent to the people of Ad; Salih (AS) to Thamud; Shuaib (AS) to Madyan.
- Yusuf (AS): Surah Yusuf tells his story in one continuous narrative.
- Al-Kahf: the people of the cave, Musa (AS) and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn.
- Ayat al-Kursi is in Surah Al-Baqarah; Surah Al-Ikhlas states the oneness of Allah.
- Al-Hujurat teaches manners: no mocking, backbiting or suspicion. Al-Asr says people are in loss except those who believe, do good and urge one another to truth and patience.
> Which statement about the compilation of the Quran is correct?
> (A) Uthman (RA) first wrote the Quran down  (B) Abu Bakr (RA) had it collected into one copy after Yamamah  (C) It was first compiled under the Umayyads  (D) Hafsa (RA) wrote the first copy herself
> B. The Quran was written down in the Prophet's (PBUH) lifetime; Abu Bakr (RA) gathered it into one volume, Hafsa (RA) kept that copy, and Uthman (RA) later had standard copies made.
> Which surah was revealed in Madinah?  (A) Al-Alaq  (B) Yasin  (C) Al-Baqarah  (D) Al-Kahf
> C. Al-Baqarah deals with laws and community life and is Madani; the others are Makki.
## Traps
! Uthman (RA) did not compose or first collect the Quran; he standardised copies of the collection made under Abu Bakr (RA).
! The first revelation was in Ramadan, but the Hijrah and the Islamic calendar came much later. Do not mix the two dates.
! Al-Fatiha is first in order, but it was not the first revelation; that was the start of Al-Alaq.
## Quick check
- 114 surahs, 30 paras, about 23 years of revelation.
- First revelation: Hira, Ramadan, Al-Alaq, age about 40.
- Compilation: Abu Bakr (RA) and Zayd ibn Thabit (RA); copy with Hafsa (RA); standard copies by Uthman (RA).
- Tawrat–Musa, Zabur–Dawud, Injil–Isa, Quran–Muhammad (PBUH).
